missing: How each charger splits its power when all three devices are plugged in. The shopper needs to know which chargers keep a full 140W for the MacBook while the iPhone (about 27W+) and iPad (about 35–45W) also charge at full speed. That takes roughly 200W or more of total output. No source tests this or gives current prices.
why: One major reviewer, Macworld, answers this with its own reviews. It reviews multi-port chargers for the 16-inch MacBook Pro, including 200W desktop chargers that keep 140W PD 3.1. GearExplained, a niche site, gives a direct pick but shows no testing. Everything else misses the question: the Tom's Guide pages, TechRadar and Digital Camera World cover other topics, two Apple pages are dead, and the Anker listing has no power-split detail. A new page could get in, but it would be competing with Macworld. The opening is a split-by-split table showing what each charger delivers with all three devices plugged in.
